body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal F_s\) and every smooth four-density path with tangent \(\delta\), the selected lifted map \(P\mapsto(\widetilde T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\) is Fr\'echet differentiable and its derivative is exactly the corrected operator \(\mathcal D_P[\delta]\) in def:nested-derivative.  Explicitly, its harmonic part is
\[
\mathcal H_P[\delta]
=\left(
b_T+\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
\operatorname{div}(B b_T)
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\left(
b_p+\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
\operatorname{div}(\mathsf C b_p)
\right)
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J},
\]
where \(b_p=\dot a_p\) and \(b_T=\dot a_T\) are determined by the differentiated reduced-cost stationarity equations.  The remaining scalar part is
\[
\left(
\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0
[\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})+e_{T0}-e_{T1}]
-\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
The coefficient identity \(BD^{-\mathsf T}=\alpha\mathsf C\) holds.  The two augmented scalar--harmonic systems are uniformly invertible over \(\mathcal F_s\), and the maps \(\delta\mapsto(b_p,b_T)\) have cellwise Riesz scores with uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) norms.  Consequently \(\mathcal H_P\) contributes \(O(1/\log(1/h))\) to \(\Sigma_h(P)\), and its cross-covariance with the Green score is \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\), uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\).  This extends the one-target fixed-source density-curve derivative in GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization to a four-input nested map with a generated target law and nonzero harmonic translation modes.
body.justification: The weighted-Hodge Schur complement proves uniform harmonic invertibility, determines both nonzero translation derivatives, and yields the exact corrected four-input decomposition.
body.gap: The frozen formula omitted the scalar elliptic correctors generated by the inner and outer harmonic velocities; this bundle supplies the required formal correction and proof without a new assumption.
body.consumer: Every finite-bandwidth score and adjoint implementation must use the corrected coefficient-divergence terms.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(f=f_{C0}\) and \(g=f_{C1}\) for the inner problem.  We first prove the scalar--harmonic linearization for a generic selected no-cut transport
\[
 F(x)=x+a+\nabla\phi(x),\qquad F\#(f\,dx)=g\,dx,qquad \int_{\mathbb T^2}\phi=0.
\tag{1}
\]
By ass:density-positivity and the applicable one of ass:inner-ellipticity and ass:outer-ellipticity,
\[
 c\leq f\leq C,qquad \lambda I_2\preceq DF\preceq\Lambda I_2.
\tag{2}
\]
Consequently the symmetric coefficient \(A_F=f(DF)^{-1}\) satisfies
\[
 \frac c\Lambda I_2\preceq A_F\preceq\frac C\lambda I_2.
\tag{3}
\]
On the space of mean-zero periodic functions, the energy
\(u\mapsto\frac12\int\nabla u^{\mathsf T}A_F\nabla u-\langle r,u\rangle\)
is strictly convex and coercive by (3) and the periodic Poincar\'e inequality.  Minimization over finite Fourier sums followed by completion therefore constructs the unique weak solution of
\(-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u)=r\), for every mean-zero \(r\in H^{-1}\), and testing the Galerkin equations before passage to the limit gives
\[
 \lVert\nabla u\rVert_2\leq C\lVert r\rVert_{H^{-1}}.
\tag{4}
\]

The finite-dimensional equation comes from transport optimality.  Ass:lift-regularity places the graph in one smooth squared-distance chart.  In that chart use the Lagrangian
\[
 \mathcal K(F,\eta)=\frac12\int|F(x)-x|^2f(x)\,dx
 +\int\eta(F(x))f(x)\,dx-\int\eta(y)g(y)\,dy.
\tag{5}
\]
Stationarity in \(F\) and differentiation in \(x\) give, respectively,
\[
 \nabla\eta(F(x))=x-F(x),
 \qquad I_2+D^2\eta(F(x))=(DF(x))^{-1}.
\tag{6}
\]
For a harmonic velocity \(b\in\mathbb R^2\), write its feasible velocity as
\[
 v_b=b+\nabla\psi_b,qquad \int\psi_b=0.
\tag{7}
\]
Differentiating \(g(F)\det DF=f\), with \(f,g\) fixed, and using the Piola identity yields
\[
 \operatorname{div}(A_Fv_b)=0,
 \qquad -\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla\psi_b)=\operatorname{div}(A_Fb).
\tag{8}
\]
Thus (4) uniquely determines \(\psi_b\).  Let \(J_F(a;f,g)\) be the transport cost after the scalar mass equation has been solved at fixed \(a\).  At the stationary value of \(a\), equations (6)--(8) give the reduced Hessian identity
\[
 b^{\mathsf T}D_a^2J_F(a;f,g)b
 =\int v_b^{\mathsf T}A_Fv_b
 =\inf_{\substack{\psi\ {
m periodic}\\ \int\psi=0}}
   \int(b+\nabla\psi)^{\mathsf T}A_F(b+\nabla\psi).
\tag{9}
\]
Indeed, (8) is the Euler equation of the displayed energy, while the first equality follows by differentiating (5) twice and substituting (6); all acceleration terms vanish by the first-order equations.  Since \(\int\nabla\psi_b=0\), (3) and (9) imply
\[
 b^{\mathsf T}D_a^2J_F(a;f,g)b
 \geq\frac c\Lambda\int|b+\nabla\psi_b|^2
 =\frac c\Lambda\bigl(|b|^2+\lVert\nabla\psi_b\rVert_2^2\bigr)
 \geq\frac c\Lambda|b|^2.
\tag{10}
\]
This is uniform harmonic coercivity and uses no additional nondegeneracy assumption.

Let \((f_t,g_t)\) be a smooth density path and write \((\dot f,\dot g)\) for its tangent.  Decompose
\(\dot F=b_F+\nabla u_F\), with \(\int u_F=0\).  Differentiation of the mass equation gives
\[
 \dot f=\det(DF)\dot g\circ F+
 \operatorname{div}\{A_F(b_F+\nabla u_F)\}.
\tag{11}
\]
Hence, for \(r_F=\det(DF)\dot g\circ F-\dot f\),
\[
 -\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u_F)
 =r_F+\operatorname{div}(A_Fb_F).
\tag{12}
\]
The right side integrates to zero.  Define the density-forcing vector by
\[
 d^{\mathsf T}\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g]
 :=\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_{t=0}D_aJ_F(a;f_t,g_t)[d],
 \qquad d\in\mathbb R^2.
\tag{13}
\]
Differentiating the two reduced stationarity equations gives
\[
 D_a^2J_F(a;f,g)b_F=-\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g],
 \qquad
 b_F=-\{D_a^2J_F(a;f,g)\}^{-1}\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g].
\tag{14}
\]
Equations (4), (10), (12), and (14) prove uniform invertibility of the augmented scalar--harmonic system.

We also need the asserted Riesz bound.  Differentiate (5) once in the density path and once in the harmonic direction \(d\).  By (6) and (11), all derivatives of the constrained map cancel.  The remaining terms are integrals of \(\dot f\) or \(\dot g\) against uniformly smooth functions and the energy pairing
\[
 \int v_d^{\mathsf T}A_F\nabla u_0,
 \qquad -\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u_0)=r_F.
\tag{15}
\]
Changing variables by \(F\), then applying (4), (9), and Cauchy--Schwarz, proves
\[
 |\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g]|
 \leq C\left(
 \left\lVert\frac{\dot f}{f}\right\rVert_{L^2(f)}+
 \left\lVert\frac{\dot g}{g}\right\rVert_{L^2(g)}
 \right).
\tag{16}
\]
Solving the scalar adjoint in (12) and the two finite-dimensional adjoints in (14), and integrating (13) by parts, therefore gives functions \(\zeta_{F,f}\) and \(\zeta_{F,g}\) such that every coordinate of \(b_F\) equals
\[
 \int\zeta_{F,f}\dot f+\int\zeta_{F,g}\dot g,
 \qquad
 \lVert\zeta_{F,f}\rVert_{L^2(f)}+
 \lVert\zeta_{F,g}\rVert_{L^2(g)}\leq C.
\tag{17}
\]
Uniformity follows from (2)--(3), the uniform density smoothness bound, and the common branch margin.

Apply the system first to \(p\).  With \(A=f_{C0}S^{-1}\), \(b_p=\dot a_p\), and scalar derivative \(u_p\),
\[
 \mathcal L_Au_p=\det(S)\delta_{C1}\circ p-\delta_{C0}
 +\operatorname{div}(Ab_p).
\tag{18}
\]
In treated-post coordinates take the mean-zero representative of
\[
 \bar u_p(y)=b_p^{\mathsf T}\{R_0(y)-y\}+u_p(R_0(y)).
\tag{19}
\]
Equivariance makes this expression periodic up to an additive constant, and the chain rule gives
\[
 b_p+\nabla\bar u_p(y)=D(y)^{\mathsf T}
 \{b_p+\nabla u_p(R_0(y))\}.
\tag{20}
\]
The Piola change of variables in (18) now yields
\[
 \mathcal L_{\mathsf C}\bar u_p
 =e_{C1}-e_{C0}+\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p).
\tag{21}
\]

The generated law must also be differentiated.  For every smooth periodic \(\zeta\),
\[
 \left.\frac d{dt}\right|_0\int\zeta\,dq_t
 =\int\zeta(p(x))\delta_{T0}(x)\,dx
 +\int\nabla\zeta(p(x))^{\mathsf T}
     \{b_p+\nabla u_p(x)\}f_{T0}(x)\,dx.
\tag{22}
\]
Changing variables and integrating by parts gives
\[
 \dot q=p\#\delta_{T0}
 -\operatorname{div}_z\!left[q(z)
 \{b_p+\nabla u_p\}(p^{-1}(z))\right].
\tag{23}
\]
Pulling (23) through \(T\) and using (20) gives
\[
 \det(H)\dot q\circ T=e_{T0}-
 \operatorname{div}\!left[BD^{-\mathsf T}
 \{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}\right].
\tag{24}
\]
The population mass equation for \(R_0\) is
\[
 f_{T1}(y)=f_{T0}(R_0(y))\det D(y).
\tag{25}
\]
Using \(D=S(R_0)^{-1}H\) and symmetry of \(S,H\), direct multiplication gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \alpha\mathsf C
 &=\frac{f_{T0}(R_0)}{f_{C0}(R_0)}\det(D)D^{-1}
   \{f_{C0}(R_0)S(R_0)^{-1}\}D^{-\mathsf T}\\
 &=f_{T1}H^{-1}S(R_0)H^{-1}=BD^{-\mathsf T}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
No commutation of \(S\) and \(H\) is used.  Combining (21), (24), (26), and the product rule yields
\[
 \det(H)\dot q\circ T=e_{T0}+\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}.
\tag{27}
\]
Apply the augmented system to \(T\).  With \(b_T=\dot a_T\) and scalar derivative \(u_T\),
\[
 \mathcal L_Bu_T=e_{T0}-e_{T1}+\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}
 +\operatorname{div}(Bb_T).
\tag{28}
\]
By (21),
\[
 \nabla\bar u_p=
 \nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
 +\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
   \operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p).
\tag{29}
\]
Substitution of (29) in (28), followed by addition of \(b_T\), is exactly \(\mathcal D_P[\delta]\) and \(\mathcal H_P[\delta]\) in def:nested-derivative.

It remains to justify Fr\'echet, rather than only pathwise, differentiability.  Fix \(\vartheta=1/4\), let \(u=(u_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) be a zero-integral perturbation, and set
\[
 U_1=\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}},
 \qquad U_0=\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}.
\tag{30}
\]
When the \(C^{2,\vartheta}\) norm is within the common branch chart, the exact identities
\[
 \det(M+E)-\det M-\operatorname{cof}(M):E=\det E,
\qquad
 \frac1{a+v}-\frac1a+\frac v{a^2}=
 \frac{v^2}{a^2(a+v)}
\tag{31}
\]
show that determinant and reciprocal residuals are bounded in \(C^{0,\vartheta}\) by \(CU_1U_0\).  The integral Taylor identity
\[
 q(x+v)-q(x)-Dq(x)v
 =\int_0^1\{Dq(x+tv)-Dq(x)\}v\,dt
\tag{32}
\]
and its inverse-map analogue give the same bound for composition and inverse residuals.  Differentiating (5) on this chart gives the bound \(CU_1U_0\) for the harmonic-stationarity residual as well.  The scalar inverse bound (4) and harmonic Schur-complement bound (10) therefore imply, for a single map,
\[
 |a_{F,u}-a_F-b_F|+
 \lVert\phi_{F,u}-\phi_F-u_F\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}
 \leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{33}
\]
Apply (33) first to \(p\), expand the exact generated density
\(f_{C1}(f_{T0}/f_{C0})\circ p^{-1}\) using (31)--(32), and apply (33) to \(T\).  This proves
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}\left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j\right\rVert\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{34}
\]

Finally, (16)--(17), applied successively to the inner and outer systems and to (23), show that every coordinate of \(b_p,b_T\), and every smooth elliptic corrector multiplying them in \(\mathcal H_P\), has a cellwise \(L^2(P_g)\) Riesz score bounded by one common constant.  For a centered kernel tangent its score is \(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta-P_g(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta)\), whose \(L^2(P_g)\) norm is bounded by Young's inequality and ass:density-positivity.  By lem:elliptic-green-gradient-bound, with the torus localization proved in the proof of lem:uniform-critical-estimates below, the leading Green score has squared \(L^2\) norm at most
\[
 C\int_h^1r^{-2}r\,dr+C\leq C\log(1/h).
\tag{35}
\]
Thus the normalized harmonic variance is \(O(1/\log(1/h))\), and Cauchy--Schwarz makes every normalized Green--harmonic covariance \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\).  All bounds are uniform over \(\mathcal F_s\).  This proves every assertion.
